title: Dev hello pathway: pricing & sample prompts
body:
Purpose:
Create a tight, developer-first one-pager that product, docs, and growth can reuse when talking to engineers about Redwood Hosted API. This is a working draft: quick-start copy, three short value props, sample SDK snippet & prompts, and a few pricing anchor lines we can A/B test in trial flows.

Context and objective:
- Problem: engineers evaluate APIs in minutes — friction around sign-up, unclear cost signals, and slow sample paths kill conversions.
- Goal: a 30s -> 5m -> 15m pathway that gets an engineer to a meaningful integration while setting clear expectations on cost and performance.
- Audience: backend engineers, product engineers building features (search, summarization, chat), early-stage ML engineers evaluating hosted inference.

Topline developer-first value props (short):
1) Instant: start generating in under 60s with SDKs, examples, and starter tokens.
2) Predictable: clear per-token metering + pre-check cost estimator for common prompt sizes.
3) Production-ready: dev -> prod path with the same API surface, token budgets, and built-in fallbacks for latency/cost.

Why these matter vs competitors (notes):
- OpenAI: great model choices but ambiguous cost tradeoffs for long conversational contexts; Redwood sells predictability and deploy paths (dedicated/private).
- Anthropic/Cohere: strong safety/eval narratives — Redwood leans into operational levers (batching, KV cache, quant profiles) to lower real unit cost.
- Self-hosted runtimes: lower raw cost sometimes but higher ops time; we sell time-to-safe-scale and consistent SLAs.

Quickstart pathways (3 entry points)
- 30s (Hello, world):
  - Create account, copy key, curl example to get a short completion (pre-filled 32-token credit).
  - Outcome: see a generated answer and cost estimate displayed inline.
- 5m (Feature proof):
  - Run the SDK sample (Node/Python) for a summarization endpoint, feed a 800-token doc, get summary.
  - Outcome: measure latency and tokens; quick link to privacy/data handling details.
- 15m (Integration stub):
  - Add a route to an existing app (webhook or serverless), wire streaming responses, add simple retry + fallback policy (cheat-sheet).
  - Outcome: first real user-visible feature on production-ish traffic using starter-tier quotas.

Sample copy snippets to use in UI / emails (short variants):
- "Launch an LLM endpoint in 60s — same API from prototype to production. Start with free credits."
- "Clear pricing, instant cost preview — know your spend before you send the first request."
- "Need reserved capacity? Upgrade to Dedicated when you’re ready; no code changes required."

Pricing-language drafts (experiments to A/B):
A) Transparent metering (preferred test):
  - "Pay per token: generation tokens + input tokens. Preview estimated cost before you send large requests."
  - Example anchor: "A 1,000-token summarization costs approximately $0.02–$0.06 depending on model and quant profile."
B) Starter credit + burst protection (trial-focused):
  - "New accounts get $50 starter credit to try integrations; we warn at 80% of credit and show cost-for-request details."
C) Commit path framing (sales-assist):
  - "Reserved pools for predictable throughput — monthly commit discounts and SLA-backed latency guarantees."

Guidance for in-product UX elements:
- Cost preview microcopy under the request panel: "Estimated cost: ~0.03" (shows when tokens > 200).
- Early-warning banner for high spending sequences: triggers at $5/day default during trial.
- Toggle: "Show production cost estimate" — uses Dedicated pricing assumptions.

Sample SDK snippet (short, language-agnostic pseudo):
- Steps: install SDK -> set REDWOOD_API_KEY -> call client.responses.create with model, max_tokens, stream true -> handle chunks.
- Copy to surface in docs and Quickstart: include a short streaming example and a non-streaming example that returns cost metadata with each response.

Sample prompt bundle (quick to paste into console/Playground):
- Use-case: meeting-notes summarizer (800–1200 token input)
  - System: "You are a concise meeting summarizer. Produce 3 bullets: decisions, action items, open questions."
  - User: "[PASTE TRANSCRIPT]"
- Use-case: code assistant (200–600 tokens)
  - System: "You are a pragmatic Python assistant. Provide minimal code changes and tests."

Competitive hooks and positioning statements to test in headlines:
- "Engineered for production inference — predictable latency and costs at scale."
- "Same API for prototype and private deployments (VPC/on-prem)."
- "Operational controls that actually reduce cost: caching, batching, quantization profiles."

Metrics to track in these experiments:
- Developer activation funnel: 1) API key created -> 2) First successful request -> 3) First streamed response -> 4) Integration route added within 7 days.
- Cost clarity metrics: % of users who view cost preview before first large request; rate of surprise overages.
- Conversion: % trial accounts hitting reserved capacity conversation within 90 days.

Proposed experiments (first 3):
1) Homepage CTA variant: "Start in 60s with $50 credit" vs "Start in 60s (cost preview)" — measure time-to-first-request and first-hour spend.
2) In-console cost preview enabled by default vs opt-in — measure reduction in overages & neg support tickets.
3) Quickstart flows: include sample prompt bundles vs blank sandbox — measure engagement with sample prompts and conversion to integration.

Open questions / unresolved tradeoffs:
- How explicit should we be about quantized model tiers in public docs vs only in deep-dive pages?
- Default trial caps: $50 is conservative; for some flows $100 reduces friction — what's the churn impact?
- Should cost preview assume worst-case (hosted peak) or median (observed)?

Next steps / owners:
- Draft quickstart page + copy variants for homepage and in-console banners (Owner: Rohan).
- Engineering: wire cost-preview API (estimate endpoint) as a beta feature (Owner: Priya).
- Growth: implement CTA A/B test and measure metrics above (Owner: Miles).

Notes to designers/product: keep microcopy minimal, surface an explicit link to "how cost is calculated" from the quickstart modal.

Raw link references and inspiration:
- Confluence: CONFLUENCE-PLATFORM-1423 (pricing model details)
- Jira: GTM-87 (homepage copy experiment)
- Quickstarts repo PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/quickstarts/pull/54

Rough timeline: 2-week pilot for A/B tests, feature flag for cost preview, iterate content in week 3 based on early metrics.

Notes to self (working rough):
- Keep examples small and copy tight; engineers skip fluff.
- Emphasize the "same API from dev to private deployment" signal — product teams value low lift.
- Capture feedback from first 50 trials for copy + UX refinement.
